title: Avoid Public Event publisher
summary: A new community knowledge article with samples advises declaring event publishers local or internal instead of public, because the access modifier controls who may raise an event, not who may subscribe. Sample files of four existing Microsoft-layer articles drop their incidental public modifier.
key_points: Publisher access modifiers govern who may raise the event, not who may subscribe
A public publisher becomes a caller contract that cannot be narrowed after release
Use local when only the declaring object raises it, internal behind a public facade
New community article with good and bad samples
Four publishers in existing Microsoft-layer sample files lose their incidental public modifier
quote: the access modifier governs who may *raise* the event, not who may subscribe
